problem_definition.area: Network Intrusion Detection and Anomaly Detection
problem_definition.nature: Rare and critical network attacks focusing on Remote-to-Local (R2L) and User-to-Root (U2R) privilege escalation threats
problem_definition.description: This cybersecurity problem involves detecting rare but highly impactful network intrusions where attackers either gain unauthorized local access from remote locations (R2L) or escalate privileges from user-level to root access (U2R). The dataset reflects real-world challenges including severe class imbalance and subtle attack signatures embedded within normal network traffic. The attacks are difficult to detect due to their rarity and the sophisticated nature of privilege escalation attempts, requiring advanced anomaly detection and imbalanced learning techniques. Observed patterns include low duration connections with specific protocol and service usage, presence of indicators such as root shell access, failed login attempts, and unusual file creation or access activities.
problem_definition.attack_vector: Exploitation of network services and protocols (e.g., ftp_data, telnet, http) to remotely gain unauthorized access and escalate privileges through techniques like buffer overflow, rootkits, and password guessing
problem_definition.asset_targeted: Networked hosts and services, particularly those providing remote access and user privilege management on critical infrastructure
problem_definition.impact_level: High - These attacks can lead to full system compromise, unauthorized data access, and control over critical network assets

indicators_of_compromise: presence of root_shell=1 and su_attempted=0 in malicious samples
unusual service usage such as ftp_data and telnet with abnormal byte counts
flags indicating connection status anomalies (e.g., RSTO, S3)
high difficulty_level scores correlating with stealthy attacks
elevated error rates (rerror_rate, srv_rerror_rate) in attack samples
hot indicators reflecting suspicious system activity
abnormal patterns in dst_host_srv_diff_host_rate and srv_diff_host_rate
attack_patterns: short duration TCP connections with zero or low src_bytes but high dst_bytes
use of services like ftp_data, telnet, and http for attack payload delivery
presence of root shell and file creation attempts in U2R attacks
failed login attempts preceding successful privilege escalation
high same_srv_rate and low diff_srv_rate indicating targeted service exploitation
frequent SYN and REJ errors indicating scanning or brute force attempts
rare but high-impact events embedded within normal traffic patterns
normal_patterns: zero or low hot indicators and failed login attempts
balanced src_bytes and dst_bytes with standard protocol usage (udp, tcp, icmp)
flags predominantly SF indicating normal connection status
high same_srv_rate and low error rates
consistent logged_in=0 or 1 without suspicious privilege escalation indicators
normal counts of connections to hosts and services without anomalies
absence of root_shell, su_attempted, and num_root activity

risk_reduction: Implement advanced anomaly detection systems capable of handling imbalanced data and rare event detection
Deploy multi-layered intrusion detection systems focusing on R2L and U2R attack signatures and behavioral indicators
Use continuous monitoring of login attempts, privilege escalation activities, and unusual service usage
Employ network segmentation and least privilege principles to limit attack surface and privilege escalation opportunities
Incorporate machine learning models trained on curated datasets like NSL-KDD rare to improve detection accuracy
Regularly update detection rules and threat intelligence feeds to capture evolving attack methods
Conduct security awareness training to reduce risks related to credential guessing and social engineering
problem_definition.confidence_level: High - The analysis is based on a well-documented, curated dataset with detailed metadata, realistic attack and benign samples, and comprehensive feature descriptions enabling accurate problem characterization
problem_definition.data_context_notes: The enhanced data_info.yaml provides critical insights into the dataset's focus on rare and challenging attack types (R2L and U2R), detailed feature descriptions, and domain-specific attack categorizations. This rich context, combined with actual sample patterns, enables a nuanced understanding of the threat landscape and supports the formulation of targeted detection and mitigation strategies.

original_data_info.data_description:
A curated subset of the NSL-KDD network intrusion detection dataset focusing exclusively 
on rare attack types (R2L and U2R) along with normal network traffic. This dataset contains 
only attacks that appear in both training and testing sets, making it ideal for rare event 
detection, imbalanced learning research, and cybersecurity anomaly detection studies. 
The dataset includes Remote-to-Local (R2L) attacks where attackers gain unauthorized local 
access from remote locations, and User-to-Root (U2R) attacks where attackers escalate 
privileges from user-level to root access. These represent the most critical and challenging 
attack types to detect in network security, with severe class imbalance reflecting 
real-world cybersecurity scenarios.
original_data_info.data_schema:
duration: Length of the network connection in seconds
protocol_type: Type of network protocol used (tcp, udp, icmp)
service: Network service used on the destination (http, ftp, smtp, etc.)
flag: Status of the connection (SF=normal, REJ=rejected, etc.)
src_bytes: Number of data bytes sent from source to destination
dst_bytes: Number of data bytes sent from destination to source
land: Binary indicator if connection is from/to the same host/port
wrong_fragment: Number of wrong fragments in the connection
urgent: Number of urgent packets in the connection
hot: Number of hot indicators (accessing system directories, creating programs, etc.)
num_failed_logins: Number of failed login attempts
logged_in: Binary indicator if successfully logged in
num_compromised: Number of compromised conditions
root_shell: Binary indicator if root shell was obtained
su_attempted: Binary indicator if su root command attempted
num_root: Number of root accesses
num_file_creations: Number of file creation operations
num_shells: Number of shell prompts
num_access_files: Number of operations on access control files
num_outbound_cmds: Number of outbound commands in an ftp session
is_host_login: Binary indicator if the login belongs to the host list
is_guest_login: Binary indicator if the login is a guest login
count: Number of connections to the same host as the current connection in the past 2 seconds
srv_count: Number of connections to the same service as the current connection in the past 2 seconds
serror_rate: Percentage of connections that have SYN errors
srv_serror_rate: Percentage of connections to the same service that have SYN errors
rerror_rate: Percentage of connections that have REJ errors
srv_rerror_rate: Percentage of connections to the same service that have REJ errors
same_srv_rate: Percentage of connections to the same service
diff_srv_rate: Percentage of connections to different services
srv_diff_host_rate: Percentage of connections to different hosts
dst_host_count: Number of connections having the same destination host
dst_host_srv_count: Number of connections having the same destination host and using the same service
dst_host_same_srv_rate: Percentage of connections having the same destination host and using the same service
dst_host_diff_srv_rate: Percentage of different services on the current host
dst_host_same_src_port_rate: Percentage of connections to the current host having the same src port
dst_host_srv_diff_host_rate: Percentage of connections to the same service coming from different hosts
dst_host_serror_rate: Percentage of connections to the current host that have an S0 error
dst_host_srv_serror_rate: Percentage of connections to the current host and specified service that have an S0 error
dst_host_rerror_rate: Percentage of connections to the current host that have an RST error
dst_host_srv_rerror_rate: Percentage of connections to the current host and specified service that have an RST error
attack_type: Original attack type name (normal, guess_passwd, warezclient, etc.)
difficulty_level: Difficulty level of detecting this particular record (1-21, higher means harder to detect)
label: Binary classification label (0=normal traffic, 1=malicious attack)
sub_label: Multi-class label specifying attack category (normal, r2l, u2r)
